fetch.description: Web page fetching as Markdown (official MCP reference server).
fetch.notes: The `--with mcp<2` pin works around the McpError->MCPError rename in mcp SDK 2.x, which breaks the published reference servers. Version pinned; bump deliberately after review.

time.description: Current time and timezone conversion (official MCP reference server).
time.notes: Same mcp<2 pin as the fetch server. Version pinned; bump deliberately after review.

memory.description: Persistent knowledge-graph memory across agent runs (official MCP reference server).
memory.notes: Graph is stored locally next to the npx package; nothing leaves the machine. Version pinned; bump deliberately after review.

sequential-thinking.description: Structured step-by-step reasoning scratchpad (official MCP reference server).
sequential-thinking.notes: Purely local; no network access. Version pinned; bump deliberately after review.

deepwiki.description: Ask questions about any public GitHub repository (DeepWiki by Cognition; remote, no account).
deepwiki.notes: Remote no-auth connector: the operator (Cognition) sees the questions and repo names you send it — nothing else. Disable it if that matters: `uv run python connectors/enable.py disable deepwiki`.

context7.description: Up-to-date, version-specific library documentation for coding (Context7 by Upstash).
context7.notes: Remote no-auth connector: the operator (Upstash) sees the library names and doc queries you send it — nothing else. An optional CONTEXT7_API_KEY only raises rate limits. Disable: `uv run python connectors/enable.py disable context7`.

github.description: GitHub's official MCP server (repos, issues, PRs, actions, code search) run locally.

args: GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) exec github-mcp-server stdio --read-only

github.notes: Install: `brew install gh github-mcp-server` and `gh auth login`. The token is minted from the gh keyring at launch and never written to disk. Runs with --read-only (server-side enforcement); drop that flag in mcp.json if you want the agent to file issues/PRs, and rely on the mcp_permissions deny rules instead.

google.description: Google Workspace: Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Tasks, Contacts, Chat (taylorwilsdon/google_workspace_mcp, run locally).
setup: Create your own OAuth client: https://console.cloud.google.com -> APIs & Services -> Credentials -> Create OAuth client ID (Desktop app), and enable the Gmail/Calendar/Drive/Docs/Sheets APIs you want.
export GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=... and GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=... in your shell profile.
First tool use opens a Google consent page; tokens are cached locally by the server.
Optional hardening: add --read-only, or --tool-tier complete for all 120+ tools.
google.notes: Credentials go only to Google. No third party in the path. Version pinned; bump deliberately after review.

slack.description: Slack workspace: search/read channels, threads, users; posting disabled by default (korotovsky/slack-mcp-server, run locally).
setup: Create a Slack app with a user token (xoxp-...) at https://api.slack.com/apps, or use browser session tokens (SLACK_MCP_XOXC_TOKEN + SLACK_MCP_XOXD_TOKEN) for zero app install.
export SLACK_MCP_XOXP_TOKEN=xoxp-... in your shell profile.
Message posting stays off unless you export SLACK_MCP_ADD_MESSAGE_TOOL=<channel-ids>.
slack.notes: Token talks only to slack.com. Slack's first-party remote server (https://mcp.slack.com/mcp) is an alternative if your workspace has a registered app. Version pinned; bump deliberately after review.

twilio-sms.description: Send SMS through your own Twilio account (official twilio-labs MCP server, run locally).
setup: Create an API key at https://console.twilio.com -> Account -> API keys & tokens.
export TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID=AC..., TWILIO_API_KEY=SK..., TWILIO_API_SECRET=... in your shell profile.
twilio-sms.notes: The bash wrapper expands the env vars at launch so the credentials never appear in this file or in mcp.json. SMS endpoints live in the core twilio_api_v2010 service, narrowed to Message endpoints via --tags to fit LLM context. Twilio advises not running community MCP servers alongside theirs; keep this connector in its own project scope if you enable third-party servers too. Version pinned.

whatsapp.description: Personal WhatsApp: search/read/send messages via the WhatsApp Web multidevice protocol (lharries/whatsapp-mcp, fully local).
setup: Install Go if missing: brew install go.
Start the bridge once in a separate terminal: cd ~/.kiss/connectors/whatsapp-mcp/whatsapp-bridge && go run main.go — then scan the QR code with WhatsApp on your phone (Settings -> Linked Devices).
Keep the bridge running while the connector is in use; re-pair roughly every 20 days.
All message history lives in a local SQLite DB inside the clone.
whatsapp.notes: Unofficial API (ToS gray area). No third party sees anything: traffic is the normal end-to-end-encrypted WhatsApp protocol. Version pinned; bump deliberately after review.

brave-search.description: Brave web/news/image/video search (official Brave MCP server, run locally).
setup: Get a free API key at https://brave.com/search/api/ and export BRAVE_API_KEY=... in your shell profile.
brave-search.notes: Queries go only to Brave. Version pinned; bump deliberately after review.

notion.description: Notion pages and databases (official @notionhq/notion-mcp-server, run locally with an internal integration token).
setup: Create an internal integration at https://www.notion.so/profile/integrations, share the target pages with it, and export NOTION_TOKEN=ntn_... in your shell profile.
notion.notes: Token talks only to notion.com. Notion's hosted server (https://mcp.notion.com/mcp) needs interactive OAuth, which Sorcar deliberately does not do mid-run. Version pinned; bump deliberately after review.

postgres.description: PostgreSQL access with health checks and safe restricted mode (crystaldba/postgres-mcp, run locally).
setup: Keep --access-mode=restricted (read-only-ish) unless you really need writes.
postgres.notes: Connects only to your own database. The --python 3.13 and mcp<2 pins are required: pglast does not build on Python 3.14 and postgres-mcp 0.3.0 needs the mcp 1.x SDK. Version pinned.

firecrawl.description: Web scraping, crawling, and site-to-markdown extraction (official Firecrawl MCP server).
setup: Get an API key at https://firecrawl.dev and export FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=fc-... in your shell profile.
firecrawl.notes: Pages you scrape are fetched through Firecrawl's cloud. Version pinned; bump deliberately after review.

playwright.description: Browser automation via accessibility snapshots (official Microsoft Playwright MCP).
playwright.notes: Disabled by default because Sorcar already has native browser tools (go_to_url/click/type_text); enable only if you want a second, isolated browser. Version pinned; bump deliberately after review.
